name: Morocco
sources: GDP $30.2bn: World Bank NY.GDP.MKTP.CD, series MAR, 1990 = 30,179,954,775 current US$, retrieved from the World Bank API 2026-08-12.
Population 24.4m: World Bank SP.POP.TOTL, MAR 1990 = 24,375,551. The Moroccan census of 2 September 1994 counted 26,073,717, which brackets it.

Inflation 6.8%: World Bank FP.CPI.TOTL.ZG, MAR 1990 = 6.78%. Low, and low on purpose - the dirham was managed against a currency basket and the IMF programmes running since 1983 had made price stability the visible proof they were working.

Interest rate 8.5%: World Bank FR.INR.DPST, MAR 1990 = 8.5%, the deposit rate. A real rate of plus 1.7%, which is the mildest monetary stance in this region and belongs to the only economy in it that was not fighting either inflation or its own currency.

Revenue 24% of GDP: World Bank GC.TAX.TOTL.GD.ZS gives tax revenue at 18.7% of GDP for MAR 1990; 24% adds non-tax receipts - phosphate royalties through the Office Cherifien des Phosphates, and public-enterprise transfers. The 5-6 point addition is an estimate and is DECLARED UNVERIFIED; the 18.7% underneath it is transcribed.

Investment 26% of GDP: World Bank NE.GDI.FTOT.ZS, MAR 1990 = 25.79% gross fixed capital formation. The 6/20 split between public and private is NOT a published series and is DECLARED UNVERIFIED. What it states is the direction of the reform actually in progress: privatisation law 39-89 was passed in December 1989 and named 112 state companies for sale, and eight years of structural adjustment had already pushed public capital spending down. Set the lowest public share in this region and the highest private share, which is the opposite of Algeria's.

Debt 85% of GDP: World Bank DT.DOD.DECT.GN.ZS, MAR 1990 = 85.4%, total external debt stocks over GNI - EXTERNAL debt, on the same disclosed basis as the other files in this region. Morocco was the most indebted economy in the Maghreb and had rescheduled with the Paris Club four times between 1983 and 1990.

Oil 0.0 mbd: Morocco produced on the order of 600 barrels a day in 1990, which rounds to nothing at this scale. Its mineral wealth is phosphates - roughly three-quarters of the world's reserves - and this model has no phosphate.

Military 4.1% of GDP: World Bank MS.MIL.XPND.GD.ZS (SIPRI), MAR 1990 = 4.15%. The highest burden in the Maghreb by a factor of nearly three over Algeria's, and it buys one thing: the berm across the Western Sahara, 2,700km of sand wall garrisoned by roughly half the army since 1987.

Strength 7: an abstract index. About 195,000 personnel, fifteen unbroken years of counter-insurgency against the Polisario, and light equipment - Morocco fought with M-48s and Mirage F1s where Algeria had T-72s and MiG-25s. Set just below Algeria's 8 on that trade and half Egypt's 14.

Stability 62: Hassan II thirty years on the throne, the makhzen intact, no serious challenge since the Casablanca bread riots of January 1984, and a war in the south that functioned domestically as a unifying cause rather than a drain on legitimacy. Set below Spain's 70 and above Egypt's 58 and Turkey's 55.

Separatism 0.20: the Western Sahara, and stated from Morocco's side of the argument. Rabat administers the territory and counts it as Moroccan; the Polisario Front contests it in arms from Tindouf and the UN Security Council voted MINURSO into existence on 29 April 1991 to run a referendum on it. That is a live secessionist war inside the territory the state claims, which is what this field measures. Set at double Spain's 0.10 and below Turkey's 0.30, because the Sahrawi population is small and the PKK war was not.

Authoritarianism 0.65: above the 0.60 electoral ceiling, and the judgement is that Morocco in 1990 was an executive monarchy that held elections rather than a state a vote could remove. The Chamber of Representatives elected on 14 September 1984 seated a real opposition - Istiqlal and the USFP together took 27.7% - but the King appointed the government regardless of it, Driss Basri's interior ministry administered the count, and the election due in 1990 was simply postponed by referendum to 1993. Set below Egypt's 0.75, because the Moroccan opposition was genuinely independent and sometimes refused office, and well above Turkey's 0.35.

pop_growth_1990 = 2.0838%/yr. Compound annual growth of World Bank SP.POP.TOTL, series MAR (Morocco): 21,593,778 in 1984 to 23,939,414 in 1989 — the five years ending on the eve of the 1 January 1990 start date. See EconomyRecord::pop_growth_1990 in spheres-sim/src/data/mod.rs for why the window ends in 1989 and not with the single-year 1990 rate.

note: 1990 TECHNOLOGY: AUTHORED, NOT DERIVED. What this nation knew on 1 January 1990 is transcribed and sourced grant by grant, exactly like every other 1990 figure in this file, and is not read off tfp_trend - there was never a code path from the trend to the known set, and the zero that stood there was a claim about the world rather than an absence of one (BIBLE section 8 and iron rule 4, both amended 2026-08-30). THE PREDICATE IS SPLIT, and split by the technology's OWN EFFECT TYPE so that it is mechanically computable and never a per-nation judgement call. A node whose effects include MilitaryEfficiency, MilitaryStrength, DiffusionEmission or CostReduction is SOVEREIGNTY-SIDE: holding it means this nation could PRODUCE it, so operating an imported article does not qualify. Every other node is USE-SIDE: deployed and in operational use here is enough, whoever built it, because the effect such a node pays is a productivity, health or output effect and that effect is real in the country where the machine runs. Of the 48 technologies the tree lets anyone hold in 1990, 17 are sovereignty-side and 31 are use-side.

DATA-KEYED TAIL NATION. This nation is outside the 29 authored majors, so nothing here was authored technology by technology: a grant is made only where one of two named published global series supports it, and nothing is modelled, estimated or interpolated. A short list, or an empty one, is the correct outcome of that rule and not a gap in the work.

Data-keyed tail nation: not one of the 29 authored majors. Only the two series named in ruling 3 were consulted - WHO/UNICEF WUENIC DTP3 1990 and World Bank IT.CEL.SETS. Nothing was modelled, estimated or interpolated, and no other evidence was admitted. ISO3 key used for both series: MAR.
WUENIC DTP3 1990 = 81% against the 80% UCI-1990 threshold: bio_universal_immunisation GRANTED.
IT.CEL.SETS at 31 December 1989 = 700 against a threshold of any positive count: comm_cellular_analogue GRANTED.

The other 46 grantable 1990 technologies are BLANK for this nation by design, not by oversight: the 17 sovereignty-side entries are unreachable by any use-in-operation series, and no published global series was named that keys the remaining 29 use-side entries.

granted.source: World Bank WDI IT.CEL.SETS 'Mobile cellular subscriptions', retrieved from the World Bank indicator API (api.worldbank.org/v2), source id 2, lastupdated 2026-07-13. Series values: MAR, 1989 = 700 subscriptions and 1990 = 904 subscriptions. The series is a YEAR-END STOCK, so the 1989 figure describes 31 December 1989, i.e. the game's start instant of 1 January 1990: a network was carrying paying subscribers before the start date. All cellular in service at that date was analogue (NMT, AMPS, TACS, C-Netz, RTMS); GSM had no commercial service anywhere until mid-1991.

WHO/UNICEF WUENIC DTP3 immunisation coverage (% of surviving infants), retrieved from the UNICEF public SDMX API, dataflow UNICEF:IMMUNISATION(1.0), indicator IM_DTP3, DATA_SOURCE field 'WHO/UNICEF estimates of national immunization coverage, 2025 revision'. Series value: MAR, 1990 = 81%, at or above the 80% WHO/UNICEF Universal Childhood Immunization (UCI-1990) target that defines this technology's name.
